topic: Turning 26 in Georgia 2026: State Extension Rules, Georgia Access SEP, and PeachCare

title.en: Turning 26 in Georgia? Health Insurance Options 2026 | CoveredUSA
title.es: ¿Cumpliendo 26 en Georgia? Opciones de Seguro Medico 2026 | CoveredUSA

description.en: Georgia has no extension past age 26. You have 60 days to enroll via Georgia Access. Compare Marketplace, Pathways Medicaid, and PeachCare in 2026.
description.es: Georgia no extiende cobertura mas alla de los 26. Tiene 60 dias para inscribirse en Georgia Access. Compare Mercado, Pathways y PeachCare en 2026.

h1.en: Turning 26 in Georgia? Here Are Your Health Insurance Options for 2026
h1.es: ¿Cumpliendo 26 Anos en Georgia? Sus Opciones de Seguro Medico para 2026

subhero.en: Georgia follows only the federal age-26 rule. No state law extends coverage past 26. You have 60 days from your coverage loss date to enroll through Georgia Access, your employer, or Georgia Medicaid.
subhero.es: Georgia sigue solo la regla federal de los 26 anos. Ninguna ley estatal extiende la cobertura mas alla de los 26. Tiene 60 dias desde la fecha de perdida de cobertura para inscribirse a traves de Georgia Access, su empleador, o Medicaid de Georgia.

heading.en: You have 60 days from coverage loss date
heading.es: Tiene 60 dias desde la fecha de perdida de cobertura

body.en: The 60-day Special Enrollment Period starts the day your parent's plan ends, typically the last day of your birth month. For example, if your coverage ends July 31, 2026, you have until September 29, 2026 to enroll in a Georgia Access Marketplace plan. Miss this window and you wait until the next Open Enrollment in November 2026 for 2027 coverage. Georgia Medicaid Pathways enrolls year-round if you meet the work requirement, but most working-age Georgians must use the SEP window for Marketplace coverage.
body.es: El Periodo de Inscripcion Especial de 60 dias comienza el dia que el plan de sus padres termina, tipicamente el ultimo dia del mes de su cumpleanos. Por ejemplo, si su cobertura termina el 31 de julio de 2026, tiene hasta el 29 de septiembre de 2026 para inscribirse en un plan del Mercado de Georgia Access. Si pierde esta ventana, debe esperar hasta la proxima Inscripcion Abierta en noviembre de 2026 para cobertura 2027.

label.en: Employer plan (if your job offers coverage)
label.es: Plan del empleador (si su trabajo ofrece cobertura)

label.en: Georgia Medicaid Pathways (if income under 100% FPL + work requirement)
label.es: Georgia Medicaid Pathways (si ingreso bajo 100% FPL + requisito de trabajo)

label.en: PeachCare for Kids (for your dependents under age 19)
label.es: PeachCare para Ninos (para sus dependientes menores de 19 anos)

quickAnswer.en: Georgians turning 26 in 2026 lose parent's coverage under the standard federal ACA rule. Georgia has no state law extending dependent coverage past age 26, unlike New York, New Jersey, or Florida. Your four main options after the coverage loss are: (1) a Georgia Access Marketplace plan with subsidies within the 60-day Special Enrollment Period (most common path, typically $30 to $200 per month after premium tax credits), (2) your own employer's plan if your job offers one (30-day SEP window), (3) Georgia Medicaid Pathways if your income is under 100% FPL and you meet the 80-hours-per-month work requirement ($15,960 single in 2026), or (4) COBRA off your parent's plan as a short-term fallback at 102% of the full premium. Georgia is a non-expansion state, meaning most working-age adults without young children or disabilities do not qualify for standard Medicaid.
quickAnswer.es: Los georgianos que cumplen 26 anos en 2026 pierden la cobertura de los padres bajo la regla federal estandar del ACA. Georgia no tiene ninguna ley estatal que extienda la cobertura de dependientes mas alla de los 26 anos, a diferencia de Nueva York, Nueva Jersey o Florida. Sus cuatro opciones principales despues de la perdida de cobertura son: (1) un plan del Mercado de Georgia Access con subsidios dentro del Periodo de Inscripcion Especial de 60 dias (camino mas comun, tipicamente $30 a $200 al mes despues de creditos fiscales de prima), (2) el plan de su propio empleador si su trabajo lo ofrece (ventana SEP de 30 dias), (3) Georgia Medicaid Pathways si su ingreso es inferior al 100% del FPL y cumple el requisito de 80 horas por mes de trabajo ($15,960 individual en 2026), o (4) COBRA del plan de sus padres como respaldo a corto plazo al 102% de la prima completa.

introParagraphs.en: Aging off a parent's health insurance plan at 26 is stressful in any state. In Georgia, it carries one extra complication: the state has no young-adult extension law, so the federal age-26 floor is the hard cutoff. States like New York (extends to 29), New Jersey (to 31), Florida (to 30), and Pennsylvania (to 30) give young adults a buffer. Georgia does not. The coverage loss triggers a 60-day Special Enrollment Period under federal law, and the clock starts the day after your coverage ends, typically the last day of your birth month. Starting in 2025, Georgia replaced healthcare.gov with Georgia Access as its state-based Marketplace, which means Georgians turning 26 now enroll through georgiaaccess.gov rather than the federal site. Georgia Access operates the same qualifying life event rules and 60-day SEP windows as the prior federal Marketplace, so the deadline structure is unchanged, but the login and plan comparison portal is different. Using the correct enrollment portal matters because a Healthcare.gov application by a Georgia resident will redirect you to Georgia Access, potentially delaying your enrollment and narrowing your 60-day window.
introParagraphs.es: Salir del seguro medico de los padres a los 26 anos es estresante en cualquier estado. En Georgia, hay una complicacion adicional: el estado no tiene una ley de extension para jovenes adultos, por lo que el limite federal de los 26 anos es el corte definitivo. Estados como Nueva York (extiende hasta los 29), Nueva Jersey (hasta los 31), Florida (hasta los 30) y Pensilvania (hasta los 30) le dan a los jovenes adultos un margen. Georgia no lo hace. La perdida de cobertura activa un Periodo de Inscripcion Especial de 60 dias bajo la ley federal, y el reloj comienza el dia despues de que vence su cobertura, tipicamente el ultimo dia del mes de su cumpleanos. A partir de 2025, Georgia reemplazo healthcare.gov con Georgia Access como su Mercado estatal, lo que significa que los georgianos que cumplen 26 anos ahora se inscriben a traves de georgiaaccess.gov en lugar del sitio federal.

introParagraphs.en: Georgia's Medicaid landscape is more restricted than most states because Georgia chose not to expand Medicaid under the ACA. Standard Medicaid in Georgia covers children through PeachCare for Kids (Georgia's CHIP program), pregnant women, and people with disabilities, but not most working-age adults. Georgia's limited expansion program, Georgia Pathways to Coverage, covers adults ages 19 to 64 with income under 100% FPL ($15,960 single in 2026, $33,000 for a family of 4) who complete 80 hours per month of qualifying activities including employment, job training, education, or caregiving for children under age 6. If your income is between 100% and 400% FPL ($15,960 to $63,840 single in 2026), a Georgia Access Marketplace plan with premium tax credits is almost always your best option. Note that the enhanced ACA subsidies from the American Rescue Plan Act and Inflation Reduction Act expired January 1, 2026, meaning the 400% FPL subsidy cliff is back for 2026. If your children are under 19, PeachCare for Kids covers them at incomes up to 247% FPL regardless of your own coverage status.
introParagraphs.es: El panorama de Medicaid en Georgia es mas restrictivo que en la mayoria de los estados porque Georgia eligio no expandir Medicaid bajo el ACA. El Medicaid estandar en Georgia cubre a ninos a traves de PeachCare para Ninos (el programa CHIP de Georgia), mujeres embarazadas y personas con discapacidades, pero no a la mayoria de los adultos en edad de trabajar. El programa de expansion limitada de Georgia, Georgia Pathways to Coverage, cubre a adultos de 19 a 64 anos con ingresos inferiores al 100% del FPL ($15,960 individual en 2026, $33,000 para una familia de 4) que completan 80 horas por mes de actividades calificadas. Si su ingreso esta entre el 100% y el 400% del FPL ($15,960 a $63,840 individual en 2026), un plan del Mercado de Georgia Access con creditos fiscales de prima es casi siempre su mejor opcion.

name.en: Confirm your exact coverage end date from your parent's plan
name.es: Confirme la fecha exacta de fin de cobertura del plan de sus padres

text.en: Call your parent's health insurance carrier or check the member portal to get your coverage end date in writing. Most plans follow the federal ACA default: coverage ends on the last day of your birth month. Some employer plans extend through December 31 of the year you turn 26. Georgia's State Health Benefit Plan (SHBP) for state employees also ends coverage through December 31 of the year you turn 26 per shbp.georgia.gov. This date controls when your 60-day Special Enrollment Period clock starts.
text.es: Llame a la aseguradora de salud de sus padres o revise el portal de miembros para obtener su fecha de fin de cobertura por escrito. La mayoria de los planes siguen el ACA federal: la cobertura termina el ultimo dia del mes de su cumpleanos. Algunos planes del empleador se extienden hasta el 31 de diciembre del ano que cumple 26 anos. El Plan de Beneficios de Salud del Estado de Georgia (SHBP) para empleados estatales tambien termina la cobertura hasta el 31 de diciembre del ano en que cumple 26.

name.es: Calcule su ingreso proyectado del hogar para 2026

text.en: Once you turn 26 and are no longer claimed as a tax dependent by your parents, you apply for coverage as your own household. Use only your projected 2026 income. Under 100% FPL ($15,960 single) you may qualify for Georgia Pathways if you meet the work requirement. From 100% to 400% FPL ($15,960 to $63,840 single), Georgia Access Marketplace premium tax credits apply. Above 400% FPL, no subsidy is available in 2026 because the enhanced ARPA and IRA credits expired January 1, 2026. The income definition is Modified Adjusted Gross Income (MAGI).
text.es: Una vez que cumpla 26 anos y sus padres ya no lo reclamen como dependiente fiscal, usted solicita cobertura como su propio hogar. Use solo su ingreso proyectado 2026. Por debajo del 100% del FPL ($15,960 individual), puede calificar para Georgia Pathways si cumple el requisito de trabajo. Del 100% al 400% del FPL ($15,960 a $63,840 individual), aplican creditos fiscales de prima del Mercado de Georgia Access. Por encima del 400% del FPL, no hay subsidio disponible en 2026.

name.en: Check Georgia Pathways Medicaid eligibility (if income under 100% FPL)
name.es: Verifique la elegibilidad para Georgia Medicaid Pathways (si ingreso bajo 100% FPL)

text.en: Georgia Pathways to Coverage is available year-round for adults ages 19 to 64 with income under 100% FPL who complete 80 hours per month of qualifying activities: employment, job training, education, volunteering, or caregiving for a child under age 6. Apply through Georgia Gateway at gateway.ga.gov or call the Georgia Medicaid hotline at 1-866-211-0950. If you qualify, Pathways provides comprehensive Medicaid coverage including doctor visits, hospital care, prescriptions, and mental health services.
text.es: Georgia Pathways to Coverage esta disponible todo el ano para adultos de 19 a 64 anos con ingresos inferiores al 100% del FPL que completan 80 horas por mes de actividades calificadas: empleo, capacitacion laboral, educacion, voluntariado o cuidado de un nino menor de 6 anos. Solicite a traves de Georgia Gateway en gateway.ga.gov o llame a la linea directa de Medicaid de Georgia al 1-866-211-0950.

name.en: Check your employer plan if your job offers coverage
name.es: Verifique el plan de su empleador si su trabajo ofrece cobertura

text.en: Aging off a parent's plan is a qualifying life event under your own employer's plan, giving you a 30-day Special Enrollment Period to enroll in job-based coverage. Contact your HR department and ask about the 30-day SEP. Compare the employer plan's monthly premium, annual deductible, and provider network against a subsidized Georgia Access Marketplace plan. If the employer plan costs more than 9.96% of your 2026 household income for self-only coverage, the plan is not considered affordable under ACA rules and you may still be eligible for Marketplace subsidies.
text.es: Salir del plan de los padres es un evento calificador de vida bajo el plan de su propio empleador, dando una ventana SEP de 30 dias para inscribirse en cobertura laboral. Contacte a su departamento de recursos humanos y pregunte sobre el SEP de 30 dias. Compare la prima mensual, el deducible anual y la red de proveedores del plan del empleador con un plan del Mercado de Georgia Access con subsidios.

name.en: Enroll through Georgia Access Marketplace within 60 days
name.es: Inscribase a traves del Mercado Georgia Access dentro de 60 dias

text.en: Apply at georgiaaccess.gov. Select the Special Enrollment Period option and choose 'loss of dependent coverage' as your qualifying life event. Enter the date your parent's coverage ended. The system will show you available plans and calculate your premium tax credit based on your projected 2026 income. Most Georgians turning 26 with income between 100% and 400% FPL qualify for tax credits. Bronze plans with credits often cost $0 to $50 per month. Silver plans typically run $30 to $150 per month after credits for a single 26-year-old.
text.es: Solicite en georgiaaccess.gov. Seleccione la opcion de Periodo de Inscripcion Especial y elija 'perdida de cobertura de dependiente' como su evento calificador de vida. Ingrese la fecha en que termino la cobertura de sus padres. El sistema le mostrara los planes disponibles y calculara su credito fiscal de prima basado en su ingreso proyectado 2026.

name.en: Gather required documents before you apply
name.es: Reuna los documentos requeridos antes de solicitar

text.en: Georgia Access and the Georgia Pathways program both require documentation of the qualifying life event. Have ready: a letter from your parent's insurer or HR confirming your coverage end date, your birth certificate or government-issued ID, your Social Security number, your Georgia address, and your most recent pay stub or income documentation for subsidy or Medicaid eligibility. Submitting complete documentation at the time of application prevents denials that reset your 60-day SEP window.
text.es: Georgia Access y el programa Georgia Pathways requieren documentacion del evento calificador de vida. Tenga listo: una carta del asegurador de sus padres o recursos humanos confirmando su fecha de fin de cobertura, su acta de nacimiento o identificacion emitida por el gobierno, su numero de Seguro Social, su direccion en Georgia y su tallon de pago mas reciente o documentacion de ingresos para la elegibilidad de subsidio o Medicaid.

name.en: If you have children under 19, apply them for PeachCare for Kids
name.es: Si tiene hijos menores de 19 anos, inscribalos en PeachCare para Ninos

text.en: PeachCare for Kids is Georgia's CHIP program, covering uninsured children under age 19 at household incomes from 134% to 247% FPL ($44,154 to $81,510 for a family of 4 in 2026). PeachCare enrollment is year-round through Georgia Gateway at gateway.ga.gov. Premiums are $0 to $35 per month. Your children may qualify for PeachCare even if you do not qualify for Medicaid yourself.
text.es: PeachCare para Ninos es el programa CHIP de Georgia, que cubre a ninos sin seguro menores de 19 anos con ingresos del hogar del 134% al 247% del FPL ($44,154 a $81,510 para una familia de 4 en 2026). La inscripcion en PeachCare es todo el ano a traves de Georgia Gateway en gateway.ga.gov. Las primas son de $0 a $35 al mes.

footnote.en: Georgia does not have a state law extending dependent coverage past age 26. Georgia is a non-expansion Medicaid state, so standard Medicaid does not cover most working-age adults without children or disabilities. Georgia Pathways is the only Medicaid pathway for most 26-year-olds, and only at income under 100% FPL. The ACA subsidy cliff at 400% FPL returned January 1, 2026 after enhanced PTCs from ARPA and IRA expired. Income uses MAGI definition.
footnote.es: Georgia no tiene una ley estatal que extienda la cobertura de dependientes mas alla de los 26 anos. Georgia es un estado de no expansion de Medicaid, por lo que el Medicaid estandar no cubre a la mayoria de los adultos en edad de trabajar sin hijos o discapacidades. Georgia Pathways es el unico camino de Medicaid para la mayoria de los jovenes de 26 anos, y solo con ingresos inferiores al 100% del FPL. El precipicio del subsidio ACA al 400% del FPL regreso el 1 de enero de 2026.

intro.en: The most expensive mistakes Georgians make when turning 26 and aging off a parent's plan:
intro.es: Los errores mas costosos que cometen los georgianos al cumplir 26 anos y salir del plan de sus padres:

items.en: Assuming Georgia has a state extension law past age 26. Georgia follows only the federal ACA floor of age 26. There is no Young Adult Option or similar program. Once your parent's coverage ends, you must act within the 60-day SEP window or wait for the next Open Enrollment in November 2026.
items.es: Asumir que Georgia tiene una ley de extension estatal mas alla de los 26 anos. Georgia sigue solo el piso federal del ACA de los 26 anos. No existe la Opcion para Jovenes Adultos ni ningun programa similar. Una vez que termine la cobertura de sus padres, debe actuar dentro de la ventana SEP de 60 dias.

items.en: Using healthcare.gov instead of Georgia Access. Starting in 2025, Georgia runs its own state-based Marketplace at georgiaaccess.gov. Applying through healthcare.gov as a Georgia resident redirects you and may delay enrollment. Go directly to georgiaaccess.gov for your SEP application.
items.es: Usar healthcare.gov en lugar de Georgia Access. A partir de 2025, Georgia administra su propio Mercado estatal en georgiaaccess.gov. Solicitar a traves de healthcare.gov como residente de Georgia lo redirige y puede retrasar la inscripcion. Vaya directamente a georgiaaccess.gov para su solicitud SEP.

items.en: Defaulting to COBRA without comparing. COBRA charges 102% of the full premium including both employer and employee share, often $500 to $900 per month for a 26-year-old on a parent's family plan. Georgia Access Marketplace plans with premium tax credits almost always cost less, particularly for incomes under 400% FPL.
items.es: Recurrir a COBRA sin comparar. COBRA cobra el 102% de la prima completa incluyendo la parte del empleador y del empleado, a menudo $500 a $900 al mes para un joven de 26 anos en el plan familiar de los padres. Los planes del Mercado de Georgia Access con creditos fiscales de prima casi siempre cuestan menos.

items.en: Reporting parents' income when applying for Georgia Access subsidies. Once you are 26 and no longer claimed as a tax dependent, apply as your own household using only your projected 2026 income. Most early-career Georgians qualify for significant premium tax credits based on their own income alone.
items.es: Reportar el ingreso de los padres al solicitar subsidios de Georgia Access. Una vez que tenga 26 anos y no sea reclamado como dependiente fiscal, solicite como su propio hogar usando solo su ingreso proyectado 2026. La mayoria de los georgianos al inicio de su carrera califican para creditos fiscales de prima significativos basados en su propio ingreso.

items.en: Not checking Georgia Pathways Medicaid if income is near 100% FPL. Georgians with income under $15,960 single (100% FPL 2026) who complete 80 qualifying hours per month can enroll in Georgia Pathways year-round for free comprehensive coverage. Many young Georgians in gig work, part-time jobs, or early-career positions qualify but skip this check.
items.es: No verificar Georgia Medicaid Pathways si el ingreso esta cerca del 100% del FPL. Los georgianos con ingresos inferiores a $15,960 individual (100% FPL 2026) que completan 80 horas calificadas por mes pueden inscribirse en Georgia Pathways todo el ano para cobertura integral gratuita.

items.en: Missing the 60-day SEP window. Without a qualifying event, Georgians who miss the 60-day window must wait until the Open Enrollment Period starting November 1, 2026 for 2027 coverage. One emergency room visit during a coverage gap in Georgia can generate a bill of $3,000 to $20,000 before any negotiated rate applies.
items.es: Perder la ventana SEP de 60 dias. Sin un evento calificador, los georgianos que pierdan la ventana de 60 dias deben esperar hasta el Periodo de Inscripcion Abierta que comienza el 1 de noviembre de 2026 para cobertura 2027. Una sola visita a urgencias durante una brecha de cobertura puede generar una factura de $3,000 a $20,000.

heading.en: Georgia Has No State Extension Law: What That Means for You in 2026
heading.es: Georgia No Tiene Ley de Extension Estatal: Que Significa Eso para Usted en 2026

paragraphs.en: Federal ACA law (Section 2714 of the Public Health Service Act, implemented at 26 USC 9831) requires all health plans offering dependent coverage to extend that coverage to children until age 26. This federal rule applies to all plan types: fully insured employer plans, self-funded employer plans, Marketplace plans, and Medicaid managed care. Georgia has NOT enacted any state law extending dependent coverage past age 26. The states that have enacted extensions are New York (to age 29), New Jersey (to 31), Florida (to 30), Pennsylvania (to 30), Wisconsin (to 27 for full-time students), and a handful of others. Georgia is not among them. The Georgia Commissioner of Insurance and Safety Fire has not issued any administrative rule or guidance extending this deadline beyond the federal floor. The Georgia State Health Benefit Plan (SHBP), which covers state and public school employees, uses a more generous calendar-year cutoff: dependent children of SHBP members keep coverage through December 31 of the year they turn 26. This does not extend coverage past age 26; it just ensures you get through the full calendar year. For SHBP members' children turning 26 in January, this means coverage through December 31 of the same year.
paragraphs.es: La ley federal ACA requiere que todos los planes de salud que ofrecen cobertura de dependientes extiendan esa cobertura a los hijos hasta los 26 anos. Georgia NO ha promulgado ninguna ley estatal que extienda la cobertura de dependientes mas alla de los 26 anos. Los estados que han promulgado extensiones son Nueva York (hasta los 29), Nueva Jersey (hasta los 31), Florida (hasta los 30), Pensilvania (hasta los 30), Wisconsin (hasta los 27 para estudiantes de tiempo completo), y algunos otros. Georgia no se encuentra entre ellos. El Plan de Beneficios de Salud del Estado de Georgia (SHBP) usa un corte de fin de ano calendario mas generoso: los hijos dependientes de los miembros del SHBP mantienen la cobertura hasta el 31 de diciembre del ano en que cumplen 26 anos. Esto no extiende la cobertura mas alla de los 26; simplemente garantiza que se llegue al final del ano calendario.

paragraphs.en: For Georgians who were hoping for a state extension, the practical implication is: the 60-day Special Enrollment Period after aging off the parent's plan is your primary window for securing new coverage. Georgia Access Marketplace plans are available within that 60-day window. The important nuance for Georgia is that coverage loss triggers a qualifying life event on both the Marketplace side (60-day SEP) and the employer side (30-day SEP if your job offers coverage). The 60-day clock starts from the actual coverage loss date, not from your 26th birthday. Knowing your exact coverage end date from your parent's insurer is the single most important first step.
paragraphs.es: Para los georgianos que esperaban una extension estatal, la implicacion practica es: el Periodo de Inscripcion Especial de 60 dias despues de salir del plan de los padres es su ventana principal para asegurar nueva cobertura. Los planes del Mercado de Georgia Access estan disponibles dentro de esa ventana de 60 dias. El matiz importante para Georgia es que la perdida de cobertura activa un evento calificador de vida tanto en el lado del Mercado (SEP de 60 dias) como en el lado del empleador (SEP de 30 dias si su trabajo ofrece cobertura).

heading.en: Georgia Medicaid in 2026: Pathways, PeachCare, and the Non-Expansion Gap
heading.es: Medicaid de Georgia en 2026: Pathways, PeachCare y la Brecha de No Expansion

paragraphs.en: Georgia is one of 10 states that have not expanded Medicaid under the ACA as of 2026. Standard Medicaid in Georgia covers specific categories: children through PeachCare for Kids (incomes up to 247% FPL), pregnant women, parents with very low incomes, and people with disabilities or in need of long-term care. Most working-age adults without minor children are not eligible for standard Georgia Medicaid regardless of income. Georgia's answer to the Medicaid expansion gap is Georgia Pathways to Coverage, a limited program authorized under a Section 1115 waiver and extended through December 31, 2026. Georgia Pathways covers adults ages 19 to 64 with income under 100% FPL ($15,960 single, $33,000 family of 4 in 2026) who complete 80 qualifying hours per month. Qualifying activities include employment, job training or education, volunteering, caregiving for a relative, or caregiving for a child under age 6. Parents of children under age 6 may be exempt from the work requirement in some circumstances. Apply through Georgia Gateway at gateway.ga.gov or call Georgia Medicaid at 1-866-211-0950.
paragraphs.es: Georgia es uno de los 10 estados que no han expandido Medicaid bajo el ACA en 2026. El Medicaid estandar en Georgia cubre categorias especificas: ninos a traves de PeachCare para Ninos (ingresos hasta el 247% del FPL), mujeres embarazadas, padres con ingresos muy bajos, y personas con discapacidades o que necesitan cuidado a largo plazo. La mayoria de los adultos en edad de trabajar sin hijos menores no son elegibles para el Medicaid estandar de Georgia independientemente de sus ingresos. La respuesta de Georgia a la brecha de expansion es Georgia Pathways to Coverage, un programa limitado que cubre a adultos de 19 a 64 anos con ingresos inferiores al 100% del FPL ($15,960 individual, $33,000 familia de 4 en 2026) que completan 80 horas calificadas por mes.

paragraphs.en: PeachCare for Kids is Georgia's CHIP program, administered by the Georgia Department of Community Health through Georgia Gateway. PeachCare covers uninsured children under age 19 with household incomes from 134% to 247% FPL. For a family of 4 in 2026, that means household income from $44,154 to $81,510. PeachCare premiums range from $0 to $35 per month per child. If you are turning 26 and have children under 19, applying them for PeachCare should be your immediate parallel step alongside securing your own coverage. PeachCare enrolls year-round through gateway.ga.gov with no enrollment window deadline. Children enrolled in PeachCare receive comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage under a managed care plan. PeachCare is separate from your own coverage, so your children's PeachCare eligibility does not depend on whether you qualify for Medicaid or a Marketplace plan yourself.
paragraphs.es: PeachCare para Ninos es el programa CHIP de Georgia, administrado por el Departamento de Salud Comunitaria de Georgia a traves de Georgia Gateway. PeachCare cubre a ninos sin seguro menores de 19 anos con ingresos del hogar del 134% al 247% del FPL. Para una familia de 4 en 2026, eso significa un ingreso del hogar de $44,154 a $81,510. Las primas de PeachCare van de $0 a $35 al mes por nino. PeachCare se inscribe todo el ano a traves de gateway.ga.gov sin fecha limite de ventana de inscripcion.

heading.en: Documents Needed to Apply for Coverage Through Georgia Access or Georgia Medicaid After Turning 26
heading.es: Documentos Necesarios para Solicitar Cobertura a Traves de Georgia Access o Medicaid de Georgia Despues de Cumplir 26

paragraphs.en: Applying for a Georgia Access Marketplace plan or Georgia Pathways Medicaid requires documentation of both your qualifying life event and your income eligibility. Missing documents are the most common reason applications stall or get denied during the 60-day SEP window. Gather everything before you start the application. For Georgia Access, the qualifying life event proof is a letter from your parent's insurer or employer HR department stating your coverage end date. This is called proof of creditable coverage under HIPAA Section 9831 rules and is required to validate the SEP. For income documentation, Georgia Access uses your projected Modified Adjusted Gross Income (MAGI) for 2026, not your prior-year tax return, though it may request a prior-year 1095-A if you previously had Marketplace coverage. Georgia Pathways requires similar documentation plus verification of your qualifying activity (pay stubs, enrollment confirmation letter, or volunteer certification) to demonstrate you meet the 80-hour monthly requirement.
paragraphs.es: Solicitar un plan del Mercado de Georgia Access o Medicaid de Georgia Pathways requiere documentacion tanto del evento calificador de vida como de su elegibilidad de ingresos. Los documentos faltantes son la razon mas comun por la que las solicitudes se estancan o son denegadas durante la ventana SEP de 60 dias. Reuna todo antes de comenzar la solicitud. Para Georgia Access, la prueba del evento calificador de vida es una carta del asegurador de sus padres o del departamento de recursos humanos del empleador que indique su fecha de fin de cobertura. Esto se llama prueba de cobertura acreditable bajo las reglas de la Seccion 9831 de HIPAA y es necesario para validar el SEP.

en.question: Does Georgia have a state law extending health coverage past age 26?
en.answer: No. Georgia follows only the federal ACA floor requiring dependent coverage to age 26. Georgia has not enacted any state law extending coverage past 26. States with extensions include New York (to age 29), New Jersey (to 31), Florida (to 30), and Pennsylvania (to 30), but Georgia is not among them. The Georgia Office of the Commissioner of Insurance and Safety Fire (OCI) has not issued any rule extending coverage past the federal age-26 floor. Once your parent's plan ends, you must use the 60-day Special Enrollment Period to enroll in a new plan through Georgia Access, your employer, or Georgia Medicaid Pathways if you qualify.

en.question: How long is the Special Enrollment Period after aging off a parent's plan in Georgia?
en.answer: You have 60 days from your coverage loss date to enroll in a Georgia Access Marketplace plan using the loss-of-coverage Special Enrollment Period. The 60-day clock starts when your parent's coverage ends, typically the last day of your birth month under the federal ACA default. For example, if your coverage ends August 31, 2026, you have until October 30, 2026 to enroll. Apply at georgiaaccess.gov and select the SEP option for loss of dependent coverage. Medicaid Pathways and PeachCare for Kids enroll year-round with no 60-day deadline.

en.question: Where do I enroll in a Marketplace plan in Georgia after turning 26?
en.answer: Georgia operates its own state-based Marketplace called Georgia Access at georgiaaccess.gov. Starting with plan year 2025, Georgians no longer enroll through the federal healthcare.gov. Go directly to georgiaaccess.gov to start your SEP application. Select 'loss of dependent coverage' as your qualifying life event and enter the date your parent's coverage ended. You can call Georgia Access at 1-888-687-1503 (TTY 711) for free enrollment assistance, or find a certified Georgia insurance agent or enrollment assister through the Georgia Access website.

en.question: Can I get Medicaid in Georgia after turning 26?
en.answer: Standard Medicaid in Georgia does not cover most working-age adults without children or disabilities. Georgia is a non-expansion state. However, Georgia Pathways to Coverage may cover you if your projected 2026 income is under 100% FPL ($15,960 single) and you complete 80 qualifying hours per month of employment, job training, education, volunteering, or caregiving for a child under age 6. Apply year-round through Georgia Gateway at gateway.ga.gov. If you have children under 19, they may qualify separately for PeachCare for Kids at household incomes up to 247% FPL.

en.question: What if I miss the 60-day Special Enrollment Period after turning 26 in Georgia?
en.answer: If you miss the 60-day window for a Georgia Access Marketplace plan, you generally must wait until the next Open Enrollment Period starting November 1, 2026 for 2027 coverage. The exception is Georgia Medicaid Pathways and PeachCare for Kids, which enroll year-round. If another qualifying life event occurs before Open Enrollment (such as losing a job, getting married, or moving to a new coverage area), that event triggers a new 60-day SEP. Going uninsured in Georgia is high risk: one emergency department visit can generate a bill of $3,000 to $20,000 or more before any negotiated rate applies.

en.question: Will I qualify for ACA subsidies as a 26-year-old in Georgia in 2026?
en.answer: Most do if income is between 100% and 400% FPL. For a single 26-year-old in 2026, that means income between $15,960 and $63,840. Premium tax credits through Georgia Access Marketplace reduce plan costs significantly in this range. A typical 26-year-old earning $30,000 in Georgia qualifies for credits that bring a Silver plan to $40 to $120 per month. Bronze plans with credits often cost $0 to $40. Above 400% FPL ($63,840 single), no subsidies are available in 2026 because the enhanced ARPA and IRA credits expired January 1, 2026. Use the screener at coveredusa.org to estimate your premium tax credit.

en.question: What happens to my children's coverage when I turn 26?
en.answer: Your children are not affected by your coverage loss when you turn 26. However, if your children were covered under your parent's plan and lose that coverage too, they qualify for PeachCare for Kids (Georgia's CHIP program) at household incomes from 134% to 247% FPL year-round through gateway.ga.gov. PeachCare premiums are $0 to $35 per month per child for comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage. Children under 19 with household incomes under 134% FPL qualify for standard Georgia Medicaid free of charge. Apply at gateway.ga.gov.

en.question: Is COBRA a good option after turning 26 in Georgia?
en.answer: COBRA charges 102% of the full group plan premium, including both the employer and employee share plus a 2% administrative fee. For a 26-year-old on a typical family plan, this often runs $500 to $900 per month for continued single coverage or more. Georgia Access Marketplace plans with premium tax credits are almost always cheaper for a 26-year-old with income under 400% FPL. Federal COBRA lasts up to 36 months for a dependent who ages off a parent's plan. COBRA makes sense only if you have ongoing treatment with a provider outside any Georgia Access Marketplace network, or if you have already met a large annual deductible for the calendar year and want to preserve it for the rest of 2026.

es.question: ¿Tiene Georgia una ley estatal que extienda la cobertura de salud mas alla de los 26 anos?
es.answer: No. Georgia sigue solo el piso federal del ACA que requiere cobertura de dependientes hasta los 26 anos. Georgia no ha promulgado ninguna ley estatal que extienda la cobertura mas alla de los 26. Los estados con extensiones incluyen Nueva York (hasta los 29 anos), Nueva Jersey (hasta los 31), Florida (hasta los 30) y Pensilvania (hasta los 30), pero Georgia no esta entre ellos. Una vez que el plan de sus padres termine, debe usar el Periodo de Inscripcion Especial de 60 dias para inscribirse en un nuevo plan a traves de Georgia Access, su empleador, o Georgia Medicaid Pathways si califica.

es.question: ¿Cuanto dura el Periodo de Inscripcion Especial despues de salir del plan de los padres en Georgia?
es.answer: Tiene 60 dias desde la fecha de perdida de cobertura para inscribirse en un plan del Mercado de Georgia Access usando el Periodo de Inscripcion Especial por perdida de cobertura. El reloj de 60 dias comienza cuando termina la cobertura de sus padres, tipicamente el ultimo dia del mes de su cumpleanos. Por ejemplo, si su cobertura termina el 31 de agosto de 2026, tiene hasta el 30 de octubre de 2026 para inscribirse. Solicite en georgiaaccess.gov y seleccione la opcion SEP por perdida de cobertura de dependiente. Medicaid Pathways y PeachCare para Ninos se inscriben todo el ano sin plazo de 60 dias.

es.question: ¿Donde me inscribo en un plan del Mercado en Georgia despues de cumplir 26 anos?
es.answer: Georgia opera su propio Mercado estatal llamado Georgia Access en georgiaaccess.gov. A partir del ano del plan 2025, los georgianos ya no se inscriben a traves del federal healthcare.gov. Vaya directamente a georgiaaccess.gov para iniciar su solicitud SEP. Seleccione 'perdida de cobertura de dependiente' como su evento calificador de vida e ingrese la fecha en que termino la cobertura de sus padres. Puede llamar a Georgia Access al 1-888-687-1503 (TTY 711) para asistencia de inscripcion gratuita.

es.question: ¿Puedo obtener Medicaid en Georgia despues de cumplir 26 anos?
es.answer: El Medicaid estandar en Georgia no cubre a la mayoria de los adultos en edad de trabajar sin hijos o discapacidades. Georgia es un estado de no expansion. Sin embargo, Georgia Pathways to Coverage puede cubrirle si su ingreso proyectado 2026 es inferior al 100% del FPL ($15,960 individual) y completa 80 horas calificadas por mes de empleo, capacitacion laboral, educacion, voluntariado o cuidado de un nino menor de 6 anos. Solicite todo el ano a traves de Georgia Gateway en gateway.ga.gov.

es.question: ¿Que pasa si pierdo el Periodo de Inscripcion Especial de 60 dias despues de cumplir 26 en Georgia?
es.answer: Si pierde la ventana de 60 dias para un plan del Mercado de Georgia Access, generalmente debe esperar hasta el proximo Periodo de Inscripcion Abierta que comienza el 1 de noviembre de 2026 para cobertura 2027. La excepcion es Georgia Medicaid Pathways y PeachCare para Ninos, que se inscriben todo el ano. Si ocurre otro evento calificador de vida antes de la Inscripcion Abierta (como perder un trabajo, casarse o mudarse a una nueva area de cobertura), ese evento activa un nuevo SEP de 60 dias.

es.question: ¿Calificare para subsidios del ACA siendo de 26 anos en Georgia en 2026?
es.answer: La mayoria si, si el ingreso esta entre el 100% y el 400% del FPL. Para un adulto soltero de 26 anos en 2026, eso significa ingreso entre $15,960 y $63,840. Los creditos fiscales de prima a traves del Mercado de Georgia Access reducen significativamente los costos del plan en este rango. Un joven tipico de 26 anos que gana $30,000 en Georgia califica para creditos que llevan un plan Silver a $40 a $120 al mes. Por encima del 400% del FPL ($63,840 individual), no hay subsidios disponibles en 2026 porque los creditos mejorados de ARPA e IRA expiraron el 1 de enero de 2026.

es.question: ¿Que pasa con la cobertura de mis hijos cuando cumplo 26 anos?
es.answer: Sus hijos no se ven afectados por su perdida de cobertura cuando usted cumple 26 anos. Sin embargo, si sus hijos estaban cubiertos bajo el plan de sus padres y tambien pierden esa cobertura, califican para PeachCare para Ninos (el programa CHIP de Georgia) con ingresos del hogar del 134% al 247% del FPL durante todo el ano a traves de gateway.ga.gov. Las primas de PeachCare son de $0 a $35 al mes por nino para cobertura medica, dental y de vision completa.

es.question: ¿Es COBRA una buena opcion despues de cumplir 26 anos en Georgia?
es.answer: COBRA cobra el 102% de la prima grupal completa, incluyendo tanto la parte del empleador como la del empleado mas una tarifa administrativa del 2%. Para un joven de 26 anos en un plan familiar tipico, esto a menudo suma $500 a $900 al mes para cobertura individual continua. Los planes del Mercado de Georgia Access con creditos fiscales de prima casi siempre son mas baratos para un joven de 26 anos con ingresos inferiores al 400% del FPL. El COBRA federal dura hasta 36 meses para un dependiente que sale del plan de los padres.

stateRules.rule: No state extension law past age 26. Georgia follows the federal ACA floor only. The Georgia State Health Benefit Plan (SHBP) for state and public school employees uses December 31 of the birth year as the coverage end date (not an extension past 26, just a calendar-year cutoff). Georgia Pathways to Coverage provides Medicaid for adults 19-64 at income under 100% FPL with 80-hour monthly work requirement.

Young Adult Option under NY Insurance Law Section 4305: extends dependent coverage to age 29 for unmarried adults without employer coverage on fully insured state-regulated plans. Does not apply to self-funded ERISA plans.
Dependent coverage to age 31 under Chapter 375 (N.J. Stat. Section 17B:27-46.1): unmarried, no dependents, not eligible for employer coverage. NJ state-regulated plans only.
Dependent coverage to age 30 under F.S. 627.6562: unmarried, no dependents. Florida state-regulated plans only.
Dependent coverage to age 30 under 40 P.S. Section 752.4: unmarried, no dependents. PA state-regulated plans only.

en: Missing the 60-day Special Enrollment Period window. Applications submitted more than 60 days after the parent's coverage loss date are denied for SEP eligibility on Georgia Access. The applicant must then wait for Open Enrollment in November unless another qualifying life event occurs.

Using healthcare.gov instead of georgiaaccess.gov. Georgia residents who apply through the federal site are redirected to Georgia Access, potentially delaying enrollment and causing the application to fall outside the 60-day SEP window.

Insufficient documentation of the qualifying event. Georgia Access requires a letter or notice from the parent's insurer or HR confirming the coverage end date. Missing or incomplete documentation is the most common administrative reason for SEP denial.

Reporting projected income below actual income and then failing to reconcile at tax time. Georgia Access subsidies are advanced premium tax credits based on estimated 2026 income. Significant underreporting leads to repayment of excess credits when you file your 2026 federal tax return and receive a 1095-A.

Applying for Georgia Medicaid Pathways without meeting the 80-hour monthly work requirement or without documentation of qualifying activity. Applications without proof of compliant activities are denied, and the applicant must reapply with correct documentation.
es: Perder la ventana del Periodo de Inscripcion Especial de 60 dias. Las solicitudes presentadas mas de 60 dias despues de la fecha de perdida de cobertura de los padres son denegadas para la elegibilidad SEP en Georgia Access. El solicitante debe esperar hasta la Inscripcion Abierta en noviembre a menos que ocurra otro evento calificador de vida.

Usar healthcare.gov en lugar de georgiaaccess.gov. Los residentes de Georgia que solicitan a traves del sitio federal son redirigidos a Georgia Access, lo que puede retrasar la inscripcion y hacer que la solicitud quede fuera de la ventana SEP de 60 dias.
Documentacion insuficiente del evento calificador. Georgia Access requiere una carta o aviso del asegurador de los padres o de recursos humanos que confirme la fecha de fin de cobertura.

Reportar ingresos proyectados por debajo del ingreso real y luego no reconciliar al momento de presentar impuestos. Los subsidios de Georgia Access son creditos fiscales de prima anticipados basados en el ingreso estimado 2026. Un sub-reporte significativo conduce al reembolso de creditos en exceso.

Solicitar Georgia Medicaid Pathways sin cumplir el requisito de 80 horas de trabajo mensuales o sin documentacion de la actividad calificada. Las solicitudes sin prueba de actividades cumplidoras son denegadas.
